text.p: Copper prices snapped back above the $2,200 level during late-afternoon LME trading on Wednesday, and prices concluded a mostly low-key session firmer.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau Index was 0.29 points lower at 241.34.

Copper traders said the late gains reflected the routine Dec option expiry earlier. This removed some of the volatility and uncertainty from the market as the large open interest calls remained out-of-the-money and thus passed out of the picture. Last three months business was at $2,208 a tonne, up $25 from Tuesday's kerb.

There was also little excitement at option declaration in aluminium, with calls at $1,500 declared and puts abandoned. But the forward market built on recent technical consolidation and physical interest to push higher. Profit-taking stemmed gains at $1,540, but final business was at $1,537, up $10 from Tuesday.
Nickel prices made consistent if unspectacular progress throughout the session, with the market's short-term technical objective pegged at $7,000. Last kerb business was at $6,945, up $110.
Lead prices staged a mini-rally during the afternoon kerb, erasing early losses, and last trade was at $688, up $2.

Zinc was inhibited to some extent by Tuesday's stock increase, although the overall fundamental and technical picture remains bright. Prices closed the kerb at $1,069, up $8 from Tuesday, aided by support around $1,060 this morning.
Tin hardly moved throughout most of a slow session before snapping above $6,100 during the late kerb. Three months closed at $6,115, against a previous finish of $6,080.
Alloy was assisted by the trend in primary metal, and ended at a steadier $1,368/73 a tonne.

CBOT wheat futures were higher at midsession on a technical bounce after the recent slide in prices, traders said. "A little short covering. Five days in a row down so it's giving a little back," said Skip Searcy, wheat trading specialist for FIMAT Futures. At 1112 CST, wheat was unchanged to four cents per bushel higher, with December up 1/2 at $3.86 a bushel.

New York precious metals futures were off the morning's highs near midday, ahead of a fire drill which will close New York commodity exchanges for about half an hour, traders said. COMEX February gold was up $1.10 an ounce at $371.50 midday, after recovering from Tuesday's contract lows at $367.70 to morning highs at $373.50. In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted $368.90/369.40, down from the London Wednesday afternoon fix at $370.90, but up from the New York close Tuesday around $368.40/90.

NYMEX crude hovered about unchanged levels Wednesday morning as crude's technical strength collided with bearish weekly oil inventory data in refined products, traders said. At 1110 EST, January crude was up three cents at $24.96 a barrel.

March CSCE world sugar futures clung what little gains they were able to make in early trade to close barely firmer, buoyed by light trade buying, dealers said. Activity was constrained as players remained reluctant to make a definitive move after the market's recent plunge to one-month lows. March closed 0.03 higher at 10.30 cents, setting its 10.35 to 10.26 trading range before midday. The back months finished 0.01 higher to 0.01 lower.
